editorialChecks.assessment: Custody, violence and escape form a causal opening. The new judge is distinct from Thatcher; the pig blood, dragged stones, meal trail and canoe are supported. Early gang/reform comedy supplies actual episodes.
Search bread is a character belief; threatened $800 sale explains Jim's flight. Shelter, supplies, raft, snake injury, disguise and search warning are supported. The body's identity is withheld.
The wreck's criminals, missing raft, stolen skiff and attempted rescue are supported. Jim's objections and Solomon argument remain his; no new doctrine or advice is added.

Separation, cruel dream trick, apology, intended betrayal, smallpox ruse, missed Ohio route and collision follow the primary sequence. The apology does not cure all of Huck's prejudice. The fog explanation remains qualified.

Hospitality and feud, the Testament note, Jack's ruse, wounded boys and recovered bodies are supported. Jim's hidden support and repaired raft reconnect the journey. Dawn, delayed axe sound, stars and steamboat waves retain atmosphere.

Impostors, collection, forged notice, murder/mob scene, three-night theatre fraud and Elizabeth memory are primary-supported. Sherburn's generalizations are attributed to him. Huck's recognition of Jim's family feeling remains limited and prejudiced.

The inherited identities, shortfall/gift/returned gold, kindness motivating Huck, coffin hiding place, family separation, disclosure, protection of Jim, identity dispute and storm escape retain causality. The sold family's return is Huck's expectation, not a completed event.

Pursuit, mutual accusations, failed scams, $40 reward claim, sale and letter decision are supported. Huck still believes the act he chooses means damnation; no modern moral conclusion replaces the scene.

Mistaken Tom/Sid identities, Tom's unexplained agreement, late warning of the frauds, needless escape devices, Jim's help moving the grindstone, three-week delay and armed response are supported. Tom's foreknowledge remains undisclosed here.

Shooting, Tom's wound, Jim's refusal to abandon him, doctor's solo canoe trip, Sally's care/racist exclusion and recapture are supported. The doctor prevents Jim's escape; the men's limited thanks leave him heavily chained.

Recapture precedes revelation of the prior will and Tom's foreknowledge. Jim's care does not earn his legal freedom. $40, the unrealized procession, intact fortune and Pap's body are supported. No killer, later family reunion or accomplished western journey is invented.
Framing accurately warns of slavery/violence and reserves the continuation and ending for Deep. The common final is navigation, not a management or moral takeaway.
